findings.title: Grouped multiplication is converted into a postfix star
findings.releaseBlockingReason: No practical compromise or substantial damage to current principal formulas or proofs was established. The bounded PDF presentation defect and named model/documentation limitations remain open.
findings.reproduction: Run parser-probes.mjs through the production Markdown entry point with g(x) = (x + alpha^1)*(x + alpha^k).
findings.expected: Both factors remain multiplied, as with the spaced-star control.
findings.observed: The first factor receives ^{*}; no multiplication operator remains. The existing positive fixture accepts this incorrect conversion.
findings.impact: A supported mathematical input silently changes meaning. Current normative generator equations use explicit LaTeX and were not found affected by this case.
findings.recommendedFix: Disambiguate postfix stars from multiplication using the operand type/context and add independent LaTeX/MathML expected results.
findings.requiredVerification: Unspaced grouped products and numeric products must preserve multiplication; postfix-star identifiers must retain their documented meaning. Rebuild both PDFs and compare inventories.

findings.title: Quoted ASCII mathematics loses a literal tilde
findings.releaseBlockingReason: No practical compromise or substantial damage to current principal formulas or proofs was established. The bounded PDF presentation defect and named model/documentation limitations remain open.
findings.reproduction: Compare rendered MathML for quoted a~b and quoted a b, excluding source annotations, with parser-probes.mjs.
findings.expected: Quoted characters remain distinct or unsupported characters are rejected explicitly.
findings.observed: Both quoted inputs render identically because the unescaped tilde becomes a TeX space.
findings.impact: The documented quoted-character preservation contract is violated. No affected quoted tilde occurs in the current source inventory.
findings.recommendedFix: Escape or reject all TeX-special characters in literal text according to their rendering context.
findings.requiredVerification: A literal tilde must remain distinguishable from a space; retain controls for percent, underscore, braces, backslash and caret.

findings.title: Script arguments bypass delimiter and ambiguity validation
findings.releaseBlockingReason: No practical compromise or substantial damage to current principal formulas or proofs was established. The bounded PDF presentation defect and named model/documentation limitations remain open.
findings.reproduction: Run parser-probes.mjs for x^), x_], R^(1)_0 and the rejected control R_0^(1).
findings.expected: Malformed closing delimiters are refused; the documented superscript ambiguity rule does not depend on script order.
findings.observed: Unmatched closing delimiters are accepted as arguments. R^(1)_0 is accepted with removed parentheses while the reversed script order is refused.
findings.impact: The fail-closed notation contract has uncovered paths. No such malformed expression was found in the published source inventory.
findings.recommendedFix: Validate script-argument token kinds and perform cross-script ambiguity checks after collecting the complete scripts.
findings.requiredVerification: All malformed controls must fail; explicit labels R_0^{(1)}, ordinary powers, indices and valid nested groups must still work.

findings.title: Algorithm-name hyphens render as mathematical minus operators
findings.releaseBlockingReason: No practical compromise or substantial damage to current principal formulas or proofs was established. The bounded PDF presentation defect and named model/documentation limitations remain open.
findings.reproduction: Render ascii:SHA-256(E) and inspect its MathML using parser-probes.mjs.
findings.expected: The algorithm name is rendered as literal text with its hyphen.
findings.observed: The converter uses math-mode upright letters and emits a minus operator between SHA and 256. Related HMAC/PBKDF2 names follow the same route.
findings.impact: Current PDF notation has a bounded presentation defect. The intended algorithms remain recognizable; no change to cryptographic computations is demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Render known algorithm names with an appropriate text/operator-text macro, preserving literal punctuation.
findings.requiredVerification: Assert literal names in MathML and inspect current source examples after a full document build.

findings.title: Audit index overstates the closure of AUD-006 records
findings.releaseBlockingReason: No practical compromise or substantial damage to current principal formulas or proofs was established. The bounded PDF presentation defect and named model/documentation limitations remain open.
findings.reproduction: Compare the AUD-006 index summary with the 31 retained findings/observations and their paired Markdown statuses.

findings.title: Absolute independence summaries omit fixed-point refusal
findings.releaseBlockingReason: No practical compromise or substantial damage to current principal formulas or proofs was established. The bounded PDF presentation defect and named model/documentation limitations remain open.
findings.reproduction: For an accepted container Y, consider a password candidate p for which D_p(Y) = Y. The creation refusal excludes that candidate.
findings.expected: Exact independence is attributed to the unwrapped permutation experiment; operational refusals are separately qualified.
findings.observed: Several summaries call the container fully independent of the password without that qualification, although Theorem 1 omits refusal and Theorem 2/Remark G9 account for it.
findings.impact: The statements are literally too strong in the operational experiment. This does not refute the theorem bounds; the ideal-model exceptional probability has scale 2^-256 or 2^-ENT.
findings.recommendedFix: Distinguish exact core-permutation uniformity from the operational creation procedure and link the existing refusal accounting.
findings.requiredVerification: Check all independence summaries against their exact experiment and preserve the correct suite-dependent exceptional term.

findings.title: Deniability experiments lack termination or abort semantics
findings.releaseBlockingReason: No practical compromise or substantial damage to current principal formulas or proofs was established. The bounded PDF presentation defect and named model/documentation limitations remain open.
findings.reproduction: Choose the permitted password distribution Pr[P=a] = 1. Drawing Q again while Q=P never produces a disclosure. Rare creation-redraw failures need totalization too.
findings.expected: The experiments define outcomes for all allowed distributions, or explicitly assume sufficient termination and define failure/abort.
findings.observed: The password domain permits a point mass and the experiment has an unbounded redraw loop, without specifying the result on nontermination.
findings.impact: Theorem 2 advantage is undefined for this admitted edge case until the game is completed. A trivial right-hand bound at p1=1 does not define a missing experiment. No counterexample for terminating experiments or practical cipher attack was found.
findings.recommendedFix: Specify termination hypotheses and explicit abort/failure semantics, then state how the existing coupling terms account for those cases.
findings.requiredVerification: Check singleton and multi-password distributions, rare all-refused creation cases, and the revised coupling without silently conditioning away failure.

findings.title: Repair-card sequencing wording differs from the implementation
findings.releaseBlockingReason: No practical compromise or substantial damage to current principal formulas or proofs was established. The bounded PDF presentation defect and named model/documentation limitations remain open.
findings.reproduction: Inspect Encryption::run: repair parity is computed before check_new_container; Sealed is returned only after that check succeeds. Latest inspected operation.rs SHA-256: 7eade1206d24691b15f3ef7985e2c4be8678a0fac17be3cfc6f13d777ed20091.
findings.expected: The description of computation order agrees with implementation, or clearly states that it is the release of the card that waits for verification.
findings.observed: The specification says the card is computed after the creation check; the implementation precomputes its parity internally and withholds it until verification.
findings.impact: This is a limited sequencing-description mismatch. No early repair-word release, incorrect card bytes or bypass of the creation gate was established.
evidence: Latest targeted implementation binding: src/operation.rs SHA256 7eade1206d24691b15f3ef7985e2c4be8678a0fac17be3cfc6f13d777ed20091; read lines245-340, output remains after check.
findings.recommendedFix: Settle the intended contract and reconcile the wording or internal sequence without weakening the output gate.
findings.requiredVerification: Keep a failing-creation test showing no card is released and a successful-creation test showing identical parity. Bind implementation checks to exact file hashes.

limitations: Full-scope specification/supplement audit with bounded execution, not a fully executed end-to-end implementation or release audit.
No machine-checked proof or independent cryptography-specialist certification. Ideal-function assumptions and physical memory/time lower bounds were not established.
No new full-cost Argon2 or eleven negative-recovery decryptions. Recorded keys and hash-matched historical primitive-verification records were reused with explicit limits.
Conformance uses a concurrently edited implementation checkout. File-specific hashes and later targeted drift checks define the examined phases; no claim is made for every later implementation edit.
No browser/terminal acceptance, heap-residue, allocator, swap, compiler-zeroization, cancellation/trap runtime or hardware-wallet run.
No release publishing, CI dispatch, fresh uncached dependency rebuild, live GitHub math-preview validation or comprehensive dependency-advisory/legal audit.

Bibliography structure was checked throughout; primary-source semantic spot checks cover the relevant cited techniques, not a new full-text verification of all83works. A pinned Hoang-Rogaway PDF endpoint returned403.
Every tracked path was inventoried. The15 archived files and59 retained audit files were checked for identity/provenance/metadata as applicable; their old cryptographic conclusions were not rerun.
Some original independent probe timestamps were unavailable. Retention records preserve null timestamps and distinguish reconstructed original outputs from later replays.
The pre-existing untracked docs/drafts/threat-models.md was excluded and left unchanged. No service handover or personal file is included.
